standard_prerequisites.name: Recursion principle for the Cauchy reals
standard_prerequisites.statement: To define a map out of RC into a type with an epsilon-indexed relation it suffices to give the values on rational points and limits and to verify the relation clauses.
standard_prerequisites.use: The whole construction is an application of this principle at source line 1080.

standard_prerequisites.name: Lipschitz map on the rationals
standard_prerequisites.statement: f : Q -> RC is Lipschitz with constant L when q close-epsilon r implies f q close-(L epsilon) f r.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the hypothesis, used for the rational constructor at source line 1107.

standard_prerequisites.name: Cauchy approximation
standard_prerequisites.statement: A Cauchy approximation is a family x indexed by positive rationals with the mutual closeness property.
standard_prerequisites.use: The verification at source lines 1097-1100 shows that the image family is again a Cauchy approximation.

core_obligations: Define fbar by (RC, closeness)-recursion with codomain RC and relation u sim-epsilon v := u close-(L epsilon) v (source lines 1080-1084).
Give the values on the two constructors: fbar(rat q) := rat(f q), and fbar(lim x) := lim(lam epsilon. fbar(x_{epsilon/L})) (source lines 1085-1095).
Check that the family defining the limit case is a Cauchy approximation, using the inductive hypothesis in the form fbar(x_delta) close-(L delta + L epsilon) fbar(x_epsilon) (source lines 1097-1100).

Verify separatedness of the relation (source line 1102) and then the four constructor clauses of the recursion, which amount to Lipschitz continuity of fbar for each constructor of closeness (source lines 1104-1116).
Read off the computation rule fbar(rat q) = f q and the Lipschitz condition, which is exactly the retained recursion condition (source lines 1117-1118).

proof_roadmap.step: Set up the recursion and give the two defining clauses.
The four constructor clauses and the two consequences.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 11.3.15 at source lines 1073-1076: every Lipschitz map f : Q -> RC with constant L extends to a Lipschitz map fbar : RC -> RC with the same constant, fixing the rationals definitionally. The author's proof (source lines 1078-1119) is a full verification of an application of the recursion principle for the Cauchy reals: it has to choose the relation u sim-epsilon v := u close-(L epsilon) v (lines 1081-1084), give both defining clauses including the rescaled limit clause fbar(lim x) := lim(lam epsilon. fbar(x_{epsilon/L})) (lines 1093-1095), check that the resulting family is again a Cauchy approximation (lines 1097-1100), check separatedness (line 1102), and finally verify one clause for each of the four constructors of closeness, each of which is a separate Lipschitz estimate in which the constant L is carried along (lines 1104-1116). The statement records only the extension property.
